name: Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome
definition: Lateral hip pain syndrome commonly related to gluteus medius/minimus tendinopathy with or without bursal involvement.

typical: Pain with walking/stairs or single-leg loading

investigations.MRI: Ultrasound/MRI may be used for persistent cases or suspected gluteal tendon tear.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs assess hip OA or fracture when indicated.

amber: Injection may offer short-term relief but should complement rehabilitation rather than replace it.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Kati/Shroni lateral pain phenotype may be documented as correlation only.

patientEducation.summary: Lateral hip pain syndrome commonly related to gluteus medius/minimus tendinopathy with or without bursal involvement.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
